desc:
A directed acyclic graph has n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1. Each entry edges[i] = [a, b, w] is a one-way edge from a to b with weight w, which may be negative. Two nodes may be joined by several edges with different weights.

A path is a sequence of nodes where consecutive nodes are joined by an edge; it may start and end at any nodes, and a single node is a path with no edges. The weight of a path is the sum of the weights of its edges. Return the largest weight of any path. Because a one-node path has weight 0, the answer is never negative.

n = 5, edges = [[0,1,3],[1,2,-2],[1,3,4],[2,4,10],[3,4,1]] -> 11   (0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 4)
n = 3, edges = [[0,1,-5],[1,2,-1]]                          -> 0
n = 4, edges = [[0,1,2],[2,3,5],[1,3,2]]                    -> 5
constraints: 0 ≤ a, b < n and a ≠ b; the graph is acyclic
hints: The graph has no cycles, so a best path to a node only depends on the nodes that come before it. Try to define the best path ending at each node.
Let best[v] be the largest weight of a path ending at v. It is either 0 (start at v) or best[u] + w for some edge u → v with weight w.

To use the recurrence, every u must be finished before v. Process nodes in topological order (Kahn's algorithm), pushing best[u] + w into best[v] along each edge. The answer is the maximum of all best values.
editorial: Define best[v] as the maximum weight of a path that ends at v, starting anywhere. A path ending at v either consists of v alone (weight 0) or arrives through a last edge u → v of weight w, in which case the best choice for the earlier part is best[u]. Hence best[v] = max(0, max over incoming edges of best[u] + w). The 0 option is what lets a path start fresh whenever the earlier part is negative.

The recurrence needs every predecessor of v to be final before v is computed, which is guaranteed by processing nodes in topological order. Kahn's algorithm gives that order in O(n + m): start from the nodes of indegree 0, and when a node u is popped, relax each outgoing edge with best[v] = max(best[v], best[u] + w) and decrease the indegree of v.

The answer is the maximum over all nodes of best. Parallel edges are handled automatically because each one is relaxed separately. The result fits easily in a 32-bit integer (at most 3,000 edges of weight 1,000, so below 3,000,000). A DFS with memoisation gives the same result but could recurse thousands of levels deep on a long chain.
